title: refs as a typed-open list (fix the shipped defect) + scan type/value/label + count cap

epic.name: Coordination Bus v2 (re-scoped): Repo Coordination Bus

story.as_a: coding agent posting a handoff that points at many artifacts (a dozen issues, several files+lines, multiple commits)
story.i_want_to: attach a bounded, typed-open LIST of references to a channel post instead of a fixed four-key map
story.so_that: one handoff can carry every pointer it needs (like beelink->mac-mini #812's full ref set), and no attacker can smuggle a secret through an unscanned ref key/label

rationale: This is the ONE genuine shipped defect in the coordination data model, confirmed by both the constructive and adversarial panels. `refs` is a fixed-key map `@allowed_ref_keys ~w(file pr branch commit)` (channel_post.ex:51) declared `field :refs, :map` (channel_post.ex:83). A map holds ONE value per key, so it literally cannot express #812's real handoff (a dozen issues, many file:line pairs, several commits) — the driving use case the bus exists for. Freeing the KEYS is correct, but the fix is a typed-open LIST `[{type, value, label?}]`, not a bigger map. And once keys/labels become attacker-writable, the secret/NUL scan MUST cover them: today validate_no_secrets scans only `Map.values(refs)` (channel_post.ex:304-306, the `Map.values/1` call at line 305), so an attacker-chosen ref `type` or `label` is an unscanned exfil channel onto the 30-day cross-session bus. The panel also rejected 'unbounded count with only a 16KB backstop' — keep an explicit item-count cap (~50).

background.reference: channel_post.ex:49-51 (@ref_value_max_length, @refs_serialized_max_bytes, @allowed_ref_keys), :83 (field :refs, :map), :249-274 (validate_refs), :301-307 (validate_no_secrets, Map.values scan at :305); panel agreed-gap #6 ('refs is the wrong SHAPE') and 'Free refs ... PARTLY WRONG' (drop the TYPE allowlist, KEEP the count cap, scan type/label).
background.includes: Migration to reshape the stored refs (jsonb list), a rewritten validate_refs/1 + scan over every item field, updated @derive/response shape, and MCP channel_post refs schema update.

acceptance_criteria.description: `refs` becomes a bounded OPEN LIST of items `[{"type": string, "value": string, "label": string?}]` (jsonb array), replacing the fixed-key map. `type` is a FREE string (the `@allowed_ref_keys` allowlist at channel_post.ex:51 and its key-membership check at channel_post.ex:255-256 are REMOVED) with a bounded length (e.g. <=64 bytes); `value` <= @ref_value_max_length (512 bytes, unchanged, channel_post.ex:49); optional `label` bounded (e.g. <=128 bytes). A post with `[{type: "issue", value: "#812"}, {type: "file", value: "lib/fly/auth.ex:42", label: "the failing call"}, ...]` is accepted.

An explicit ITEM-COUNT cap (~50) is enforced (panel: 'do NOT rely on only the 16KB backstop' — that is an obscure ~32-item limit and a fan-out/injection amplifier). Over the cap returns {:error, changeset} (422). The existing total-serialized-bytes backstop (@refs_serialized_max_bytes, channel_post.ex:50 — raise deliberately if needed for 50 items but keep it bounded) still applies as a second ceiling.

The secret-denylist AND NUL-byte scan now cover EVERY item field — `type`, `value`, AND `label` — not just values. Today validate_no_secrets scans only `Map.values(refs)` (channel_post.ex:305); the rewrite flattens every item's type/value/label into the scanned set so `SecretDenylist.any_contains_secret?/1` (secret_denylist.ex:80-83) sees them all, each capped at @scan_byte_cap (channel_post.ex:211-216). A secret in a ref `type` or `label` is rejected 422 exactly as one in `value` is.

Malformed items are rejected as a 422 changeset error (never a 500): a non-list `refs`, an item that is not a map, an item missing `type` or `value`, a non-string field, or an over-length field. A NUL byte in any item field is rejected 422 (jsonb cannot store it — mirrors the existing guard at channel_post.ex:261-265), never a raw Postgrex.Error.

A data migration reshapes any existing stored refs maps to the list form (`{file: "x"}` -> `[{type: "file", value: "x"}]`) so no live row breaks; the response shape (@derive Jason.Encoder at channel_post.ex:59-73 and channel_post_json/1 at channel_post_controller.ex:261-273) returns the list. The MCP channel_post tool's `refs` input schema (index.js ~2266-2296) is updated from the map shape to the list shape with a doc note on the count cap.

technical_notes: Schema/type — pick ONE coherent approach (do NOT pair `{:array, :map}` with 'column type unchanged' — they contradict: in Ecto `{:array, :map}` maps to a Postgres ARRAY column `jsonb[]`, NOT a scalar `jsonb` column holding a top-level JSON array, so declaring it over the existing scalar `jsonb` yields a Postgrex encode/load mismatch; and keeping the built-in `:map` also breaks because Ecto's `:map` rejects a top-level list on load). RECOMMENDED (keeps the existing scalar `jsonb` column, so the migration reshapes DATA only): add a small custom `Ecto.Type` (e.g. `Loopctl.Coordination.RefsList`) over the scalar `jsonb` column whose `cast/1`, `load/1`, and `dump/1` accept and validate a LIST of `{type, value, label?}` maps and reject anything else — `field :refs, RefsList`. This is the entity_definitions/dispatches convention (schema type matches column). ALTERNATIVE (only if you prefer a native array column): migrate the column to `jsonb[]` and use `field :refs, {:array, :map}` — but then it IS a column-type change; drop the 'DATA only' framing and migrate the column, not just the rows.

Rewrite validate_refs/1 (channel_post.ex:249-274): (a) refs is a list; (b) each item is a map with string `type` (<=64B) + string `value` (<=@ref_value_max_length) + optional string `label` (<=128B); (c) length(refs) <= @refs_max_items (~50); (d) serialized-bytes backstop still applies (refs_serialized_size/1, channel_post.ex:284-291); (e) NUL-byte guard over every item field.
DELETE @allowed_ref_keys (channel_post.ex:51), allowed_ref_keys/0 (:151-153), and the key-membership cond branch (:255-256). Freeing the type is the whole point (panel: drop the TYPE allowlist).

Rewrite validate_no_secrets' refs arm (channel_post.ex:304-306): replace `Map.values(refs)` with a flatten over every item's type/value/label, each run through scan_slice/1 (channel_post.ex:211-216), then SecretDenylist.any_contains_secret?/1. The @scanned_text_fields body/key/session_id/host arm is unchanged.

@refs_serialized_max_bytes (channel_post.ex:50): 50 items x (64+512+128) ~= 35KB worst case — set the backstop deliberately (e.g. keep tight but consistent with the ~50 cap; the count cap is the primary bound, bytes the secondary). State the chosen numbers as an invariant.
Response: @derive Jason.Encoder (channel_post.ex:59-73) already includes :refs — the list serializes directly. channel_post_json/1 (channel_post_controller.ex:268) passes post.refs through unchanged.

MCP: update the channel_post tool's refs input schema in mcp-server/index.js (~2266-2296) from an object to an array of {type,value,label?}; document the ~50 count cap. channelPost/1 (index.js:440) forwards refs unchanged.
Do this AFTER 40.A3 (index cleanup) per sequencing; it is the second step and the highest-value data-model correction.
